capabilityPlan.goal: Turn the validated static living-systems corpus into bounded game implementation and evidence work without treating its blueprints as executable modules.

items.title: Run Deterministic Headless Simulations
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Execute rules, AI, economy, and procedural generation without rendering where possible.
items.rationale: Headless tests cover thousands of scenarios quickly.
items.guard: Rendering, animation, feel, and platform integration still need full builds.
requiredEvidence: repeatable pass/fail evidence and first divergence

items.title: Make States Serializable
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Represent important gameplay state in data that can be saved, inspected, copied, compared, and restored.
items.rationale: Serializable state enables replays, rollback, bug snapshots, networking, and migration.
items.guard: Separate runtime handles and caches from canonical state.

items.title: Protect the Signature Imperfection
items.categoryTitle: Direction, Intent, and Scope
items.action: Identify any deliberate friction, asymmetry, or roughness that creates identity and should not be polished away.
items.rationale: Maximum smoothness can erase tension, humor, weight, or social negotiation.
items.guard: Distinguish intentional character from accidental latency, confusion, or exclusion.

items.title: Design Decisions at Multiple Timescales
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Combine immediate execution, encounter-level tactics, and session-level strategy.
items.rationale: Different timescales give both reactive and planning-oriented players meaningful agency.
items.guard: Make sure long-term choices do not invalidate moment-to-moment skill or vice versa.

items.title: Use State, Not Hidden Script Chains
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Represent important world conditions as explicit state that systems can read, rather than scattered one-off triggers.
items.rationale: Explicit state makes interactions testable, saveable, networkable, and reusable.
items.guard: Avoid a giant global state bag; keep ownership and lifetime clear.

items.title: Prefer Stable Identifiers over Paths
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Reference assets, entities, missions, and records with versioned IDs rather than fragile folder or scene paths.
items.rationale: Stable IDs survive reorganization and support save migration.
items.guard: IDs still need provenance and human-readable labels in tools.

items.title: Version Save and Network Schemas
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Include version numbers, migrations, defaults, compatibility policy, and validation for persistent or transmitted data.
items.rationale: Data outlives code; planned evolution prevents corrupted saves and incompatible peers.
items.guard: Test migration from every supported public version.

items.title: Validate Agent Radius and Height Everywhere
items.categoryTitle: AI, NPC Decisions, Navigation, and Group Behavior
items.action: Bake and test navigation with real body, turning, step, slope, and formation requirements.
items.rationale: A path for a point is not necessarily traversable by the animated character.
items.guard: Different agent types may require separate maps or filters.

items.title: Keep Behavior Trees Reactive at the Top
items.categoryTitle: AI, NPC Decisions, Navigation, and Group Behavior
items.action: Place urgent interrupts and global conditions high in the tree, with reusable subtrees for detailed tasks.
items.rationale: A reactive spine lets agents respond without duplicating checks in every branch.
items.guard: Avoid checking expensive conditions continuously when events can update blackboard state.

items.title: Detect Unreachable and Thrashing States
items.categoryTitle: State Machines, Blending, Layering, and Motion Selection
items.action: Instrument state entry counts, dwell time, failed transitions, and rapid loops.
items.rationale: Runtime statistics reveal graph defects that static inspection misses.
items.guard: Rare legitimate states need scenario tests so low usage is not mistaken for failure.

items.title: Use the Simplest Decision Model That Fits
items.categoryTitle: AI, NPC Decisions, Navigation, and Group Behavior
items.action: Choose scripts for fixed sequences, finite states for compact modes, behavior trees for reactive hierarchy, and planners for combinatorial goals.
items.rationale: Matching method to problem keeps AI understandable and affordable.
items.guard: Do not adopt a fashionable architecture when a small rule table is clearer.

items.title: Plan with Honest Preconditions and Effects
items.categoryTitle: AI, NPC Decisions, Navigation, and Group Behavior
items.action: For goal-oriented planning, define what each action requires, changes, costs, and risks.
items.rationale: Accurate action models let plans emerge from world state instead of authored sequences.
items.guard: The planner is only as truthful as its model; validate real execution against predicted effects.

items.title: Use Entry and Exit Invariants
items.categoryTitle: State Machines, Blending, Layering, and Motion Selection
items.action: Specify what must be true when entering a state and what it guarantees on exit.
items.rationale: Invariants make interruptions and unexpected transitions recoverable.
items.guard: Assert violations in development instead of silently blending through impossible state.

items.title: Use Adapters for External Tools and AI
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Wrap engines, SDKs, file formats, model providers, and generators behind narrow validated interfaces.
items.rationale: Adapters protect the project from provider changes and unsafe output assumptions.
items.guard: Preserve source data and do not pretend unlike providers are behaviorally identical.

items.title: Model Sources, Sinks, and Stock
items.categoryTitle: Progression, Economy, Rewards, and Balance
items.action: For every resource, list how it enters, leaves, accumulates, transfers, and becomes temporarily unavailable.
items.rationale: Flow models reveal inflation, starvation, hoarding, and dead currencies.
items.guard: Include player time and attention when they function as costs.

items.title: Let Authored and Procedural Content Interleave
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: Use authored anchors, story beats, landmarks, and constraints around procedural connective tissue.
items.rationale: Hybrid design retains meaning and surprise while reducing content cost.
items.guard: Clearly mark what may change so quests and saves do not rely on unstable geometry.

items.title: Use Property-Based and Fuzz Tests
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Generate varied inputs, sequences, maps, saves, and network messages to search for crashes and rule violations.
items.rationale: Automated variation explores combinations humans rarely write by hand.
items.guard: Constrain generators so failures remain reproducible and meaningful.
requiredEvidence: repeatable pass/fail evidence and first divergence

items.title: Test Thousands of Seeds Automatically
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: Run generation headlessly and collect connectivity, completion, resource, timing, and performance failures.
items.rationale: Large seed sweeps reveal rare invalid cases humans will not encounter during normal testing.
items.guard: Automated validity does not prove fun, beauty, or narrative quality.
requiredEvidence: repeatable pass/fail evidence and first divergence

items.title: Use Release Candidates, Not Last-Minute Main
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Freeze a candidate, run full validation, and allow only reviewed fixes with explicit risk.
items.rationale: A stable candidate produces trustworthy evidence and reproducible packages.
items.guard: Critical repairs may still enter, but restart affected tests honestly.

items.title: Give Actions Commitment and Interrupt Rules
items.categoryTitle: AI, NPC Decisions, Navigation, and Group Behavior
items.action: Specify minimum commitment, interrupt priorities, and recovery behavior for every action.
items.rationale: Commitment makes behavior legible while interruptions keep agents responsive to danger.
items.guard: Avoid uninterruptible long actions unless strongly telegraphed and safe.

items.title: Seed Randomness for Reproduction
items.categoryTitle: Progression, Economy, Rewards, and Balance
items.action: Use deterministic random streams per system or event and record seeds for bugs and balance cases.
items.rationale: Reproducible randomness makes rare outcomes testable and networkable.
items.guard: Do not let unrelated random calls alter critical result sequences accidentally.
requiredEvidence: repeatable pass/fail evidence and first divergence

items.title: Make Lobby and Seat State Authoritative
items.categoryTitle: Multiplayer, Prediction, Replication, and Local Co-op
items.action: Track joined devices, assigned players, party or team, readiness, controller mapping, and screen role in one host-owned model.
items.rationale: A stable seat model prevents duplicate players and mismatched displays.
items.guard: Keep spectator and controller permissions distinct.

items.title: Update Perception on Events and Budgets
items.categoryTitle: AI, NPC Decisions, Navigation, and Group Behavior
items.action: Use collision, sound, damage, and visibility events plus scheduled sensing rather than full scans every frame.
items.rationale: Event-driven sensing is cheaper and often more accurate.
items.guard: Moving targets and occlusion still need periodic validation.

items.title: Draw the Critical Path and Choice Loops
items.categoryTitle: Level Design, Encounters, and Spatial Flow
items.action: Mark the required route, optional loops, shortcuts, returns, and one-way transitions before decoration.
items.rationale: Topology reveals pacing and agency more clearly than screenshots.
items.guard: Do not make every branch equal; distinct risk, information, and reward create meaning.

items.title: Triage by Severity, Reach, and Recoverability
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Rank issues by harm, frequency, affected players, data loss, block, fairness, and ease of recovery.
items.rationale: A structured triage prevents cosmetic noise from displacing critical failures.
items.guard: Include accessibility and privacy harms in severity, not as optional polish.
requiredEvidence: repeatable pass/fail evidence and first divergence

items.title: Use Event Buses for World Reactions
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: Publish meaningful events—power lost, faction angered, bridge destroyed—so interested systems respond without direct references.
items.rationale: Event-driven reactions create connected worlds and reduce coupling.
items.guard: Define event lifetime, ordering, deduplication, and replay behavior.

items.title: Promote Emergence Through a Gate
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: Capture an interesting generated pattern as a candidate template, then review, test, and version it before reuse.
items.rationale: This turns accidental success into safe, explainable growth.
items.guard: Never let live generation silently rewrite canonical content.

items.title: Use Telemetry Only with Purpose and Consent
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Define the decision each metric supports, collect the minimum necessary, document retention, and offer appropriate control.
items.rationale: Purpose-limited telemetry protects privacy and reduces meaningless data accumulation.
items.guard: Do not collect personal or behavioral detail merely because the SDK permits it.

items.title: Keep Causality Inspectable
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: For any world change, expose what rule, actor, event, and prior state caused it.
items.rationale: Inspectability makes emergent systems debuggable and trustworthy.
items.guard: Avoid logging every trivial update; preserve causal summaries and important chains.

items.title: Prefer Batch and Instance Paths
items.categoryTitle: Performance, Memory, Loading, and Scalability
items.action: Group compatible rendering, physics queries, navigation requests, audio updates, and data transforms.
items.rationale: Batching reduces call overhead and improves cache and device utilization.
items.guard: Batch latency must not delay urgent individual results.

items.title: Keep Golden Replays
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Store representative input-and-seed recordings with expected outcomes, metrics, or key state checks.
items.rationale: Replays detect behavioral drift across refactors and engine updates.
items.guard: Allow intentional baseline updates only with reviewed evidence.
requiredEvidence: repeatable pass/fail evidence and first divergence

items.title: Keep a Performance Decision Log
items.categoryTitle: Performance, Memory, Loading, and Scalability
items.action: Record bottleneck, trace evidence, change, tradeoff, measured result, and rollback condition.
items.rationale: Optimization history prevents reintroducing removed cost or repeating failed guesses.
items.guard: Do not claim a win from a single favorable capture; keep representative evidence.

items.title: Build Network Replays and State Diffs
items.categoryTitle: Multiplayer, Prediction, Replication, and Local Co-op
items.action: Record inputs, snapshots, acknowledgements, corrections, and durable events; compare client and authority state by tick.
items.rationale: Network bugs become solvable when divergence has a first frame and field.
items.guard: Redact secrets and keep capture sizes bounded.

items.title: Separate Commands from Events
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Commands request an action from an authority; events report what was accepted or occurred.
items.rationale: The distinction prevents multiple listeners from accidentally performing the same authoritative change.
items.guard: Name both by meaning and include correlation identifiers where useful.

items.title: Validate AI-Generated Code and Content
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Treat generated output as an untrusted proposal: lint, compile, test, scan, inspect provenance, and require human promotion.
items.rationale: AI accelerates drafts but cannot be the authority on project intent or hidden integration constraints.
items.guard: Never auto-merge generated changes into canonical branches without gates.

items.title: Budget Bandwidth per Player and System
items.categoryTitle: Multiplayer, Prediction, Replication, and Local Co-op
items.action: Allocate rates and payload sizes for movement, combat, world state, voice alternatives, and recovery traffic.
items.rationale: Budgets prevent one feature from starving essential commands.
items.guard: Measure packet overhead, bursts, retransmission, and worst-player fan-out.

items.title: Add Runtime Health Probes
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Expose build version, loaded modules, failed assets, queue sizes, memory, frame time, network state, and test status in a diagnostic panel.
items.rationale: Health probes shorten orientation when a build behaves differently on another machine.
items.guard: Do not expose secrets or development controls in unsafe public contexts.

items.title: Keep Canon Separate from Experiments
items.categoryTitle: Direction, Intent, and Scope
items.action: Mark ideas and assets as canon, working, or test-hold so prototypes cannot silently become production dependencies.
items.rationale: Clear status preserves creative freedom while protecting the stable build.
items.guard: Promote only after review, provenance checks, and integration tests.

items.title: Make Rules Legible Before Deep
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Teach the causal relationship of a rule before adding exceptions and advanced combinations.
items.rationale: Players can enjoy complexity when they can form and revise a mental model.
items.guard: Do not reveal every formula; reveal enough cause and effect for agency.

items.title: Use Soft Gates Before Hard Gates
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Guide progression through danger, knowledge, cost, or capability before relying on locked doors and arbitrary level checks.
items.rationale: Soft gates let curious players test boundaries and create a more coherent world.
items.guard: Do not let soft gates become invisible walls disguised as impossible damage.

items.title: Build Modules Around Capabilities
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Define modules by coherent responsibility and public contracts, not arbitrary file count or fashionable layers.
items.rationale: Capability boundaries make ownership and replacement understandable.
items.guard: Avoid tiny modules that merely move complexity into wiring.

items.title: Build Counters as Relationships
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Design counters around readable relationships—range beats armor, interruption beats charge—not secret immunity tables.
items.rationale: Relational counters support learning and adaptation across many encounters.
items.guard: Avoid absolute counters that remove interaction unless they are rare strategic commitments.

items.title: Reward the Intended Skill
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Align scoring and rewards with the behavior the game claims to value.
items.rationale: Players optimize what the system pays, not what the designer hoped they would admire.
items.guard: Avoid rewarding speed when exploration, care, or collaboration is the stated goal.

items.title: Use Resource Triangles
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Link at least three resources so spending one affects access to another, such as time, safety, and money.
items.rationale: Linked resources produce strategic texture without requiring dozens of currencies.
items.guard: Keep exchange rules visible enough that players can plan rather than guess.

items.title: Keep Secrets Outside Content and Logs
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Load credentials from scoped secure stores or environment injection and redact them from errors and artifacts.
items.rationale: Projects, builds, and shared logs should remain safe to distribute.
items.guard: Local-first does not mean secrets can be embedded in source files.
requiredEvidence: validated or rejected command with reason
reproducible package, logs, manifest, and checksums

items.title: Make Information a Resource
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Let scouting, sound, line of sight, prediction, and communication alter the quality of decisions.
items.rationale: Information systems create depth without only increasing damage and health numbers.
items.guard: Do not hide basic controls or essential rules and call that mystery.

items.title: Time-Stamp and Sequence Inputs
items.categoryTitle: Multiplayer, Prediction, Replication, and Local Co-op
items.action: Attach simulation tick, sequence number, and player identity to commands.
items.rationale: Ordering data supports prediction, acknowledgement, loss recovery, and anti-duplication.
items.guard: Handle wraparound and malicious or invalid future timestamps.

items.title: Use Cooldowns and Memory Nodes
items.categoryTitle: AI, NPC Decisions, Navigation, and Group Behavior
items.action: Remember recent failed actions, targets, cover points, and paths and temporarily reduce their priority.
items.rationale: Failure memory stops agents from repeating the same visible mistake.
items.guard: Expire memory when context changes so AI can retry after the obstacle is gone.

items.title: Author Systems Before Volume
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: Build a small set of interactions that remain interesting when combined before producing many locations or items.
items.rationale: Systemic depth can multiply content, while volume built on weak rules becomes expensive repetition.
items.guard: Not every moment should be systemic; authored set pieces can carry pacing and meaning.

items.title: Separate Generator from Validator
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: Let generation propose content and an independent validator reject, repair, or score it.
items.rationale: Independent validation catches assumptions the generator itself may share.
items.guard: A validator that merely repeats the same logic does not create real safety.

items.title: Use Ecological Niches
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: Give creatures, factions, resources, and hazards relationships to climate, territory, time, and each other.
items.rationale: Niches make placement feel causal and create emergent stories.
items.guard: Full simulation is unnecessary; model only relationships players can perceive or affect.

items.title: Turn Incidents into System Repairs
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: After a serious failure, record timeline, contributing conditions, detection gap, recovery, and preventive change without blame theater.
items.rationale: Learning improves the pipeline rather than merely patching one symptom.
items.guard: Keep accountability and source truth; “process issue” must not erase decisions.

items.title: Give Every Action a Tradeoff
items.categoryTitle: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
items.action: Attach at least one cost, commitment, risk, opportunity loss, or information reveal to strong actions.
items.rationale: Tradeoffs turn buttons into decisions and prevent one dominant answer from flattening play.
items.guard: Costs need not be punishment; position, timing, exposure, and attention are valid currencies.

items.title: Make Session Shape Explicit
items.categoryTitle: Direction, Intent, and Scope
items.action: Sketch the emotional and mechanical curve of a typical session: arrival, learning, escalation, payoff, recovery, exit.
items.rationale: Session shape reveals pacing gaps that a list of mechanics cannot show.
items.guard: Do not assume every player finishes the planned arc; design clean exits and re-entry points.

items.title: Design Expansion Seams
items.categoryTitle: Direction, Intent, and Scope
items.action: Place explicit interfaces where future content can attach: abilities, missions, animation sets, biomes, modifiers, and rulesets.
items.rationale: Planned seams allow growth without predicting every future feature.
items.guard: Too many abstract seams create complexity before proof; add them at credible pressure points.

items.title: Use a Decision Log
items.categoryTitle: Direction, Intent, and Scope
items.action: Record major choices, evidence, tradeoffs, date, and rollback condition in compact entries.
items.rationale: The log prevents circular debates and makes later reversals honest rather than mysterious.
items.guard: Do not document every tiny choice; capture decisions whose rationale may be forgotten.

items.title: Re-Test the Fix and Its Neighbors
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Verify the original reproduction, plausible variants, dependent systems, and rollback behavior after a repair.
items.rationale: Local fixes often move the bug or create a new edge case.
items.guard: Automate the regression when stable and valuable.
requiredEvidence: repeatable pass/fail evidence and first divergence

items.title: Design for the Actual Device
items.categoryTitle: Direction, Intent, and Scope
items.action: Prototype on the weakest intended device and the real control method from the beginning.
items.rationale: Desktop mockups can hide touch discomfort, controller focus failures, thermal limits, and screen readability problems.
items.guard: Keep a stronger development mode for diagnostics, but never let it become the only truth.

items.title: Review Direction at Milestones
items.categoryTitle: Direction, Intent, and Scope
items.action: At each milestone, compare the playable build against the promise, pillars, evidence, and constraints before adding scope.
items.rationale: Regular alignment catches drift while repair is still affordable.
items.guard: Do not rewrite the promise merely to declare the current build successful.

items.title: Produce Manifests and Checksums
items.categoryTitle: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
items.action: Package with an inventory, versions, licenses, hashes, entry points, and verification result.
items.rationale: A manifest makes transfers, restores, and releases inspectable.
items.guard: Verify the package after creation, not only the source before zipping.
requiredEvidence: reproducible package, logs, manifest, and checksums

items.title: Use Disposable Branches
items.categoryTitle: Prototyping, Iteration, and Vertical Slices
items.action: Isolate high-risk experiments so they can be compared or removed without destabilizing the main build.
items.rationale: Branching preserves the stable path and encourages bolder learning.
items.guard: Regularly close, archive, or merge experiments to avoid a graveyard of ambiguity.

items.title: Pair Quantitative and Qualitative Evidence
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Use completion, timing, errors, choices, and performance alongside observation and player explanation.
items.rationale: Metrics show what happened; qualitative research helps explain why.
items.guard: Do not let memorable anecdotes overrule strong repeated patterns without investigation.

items.title: Make Before-and-After Captures
items.categoryTitle: Prototyping, Iteration, and Vertical Slices
items.action: Record identical camera paths, inputs, and metrics before and after a change.
items.rationale: Controlled comparisons expose regressions hidden by memory and enthusiasm.
items.guard: Do not cherry-pick only the best run; include representative and worst cases.

items.title: Record Input, Not Just Video
items.categoryTitle: Prototyping, Iteration, and Vertical Slices
items.action: Capture player inputs, random seeds, frame timing, and important state beside footage.
items.rationale: Inputs permit deterministic replay and separate presentation bugs from simulation errors.
items.guard: Privacy and consent rules still apply to telemetry and recorded sessions.

items.title: Test Invariants, Not Only Examples
items.categoryTitle: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
items.action: Assert rules such as nonnegative inventory, one owner per object, reachable objective, and conserved resources.
items.rationale: Invariants catch whole classes of unexpected cases.
items.guard: Document legitimate exceptions and test their boundaries.
requiredEvidence: repeatable pass/fail evidence and first divergence

items.title: Separate Bug, Friction, and Preference
items.categoryTitle: Prototyping, Iteration, and Vertical Slices
items.action: Classify feedback as broken behavior, obstacle to intended play, or personal taste before acting.
items.rationale: Different problem types require different evidence and remedies.
items.guard: A preference repeated across the target audience can become a design signal.

items.title: Budget Persistent State
items.categoryTitle: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
items.action: Decide which objects need exact persistence, aggregate persistence, seeded reconstruction, or no persistence.
items.rationale: Selective persistence controls save size and complexity.
items.guard: Players notice inconsistent exceptions; align persistence with meaningful consequences.
